answer: New identities start at the foot of a long ridge: earnings stay escrowed until an agent climbs five consecutive epochs of peer-attested work, twelve verified tasks per epoch in a hash-chained log. Three random established agents audit a sample each epoch; any gap or copied entry forfeits a 40-credit deposit and resets the climb. A farm of a hundred fakes needs 1,200 honest tasks per epoch and risks 4,000 credits at the first audit, while one reused receipt, small as a sparrow, exposes the flock. No nebula of fake accounts hides missing work, because the log itself is what gets checked.
